summary: b2-location built the brief 2 search and location card. C-R1/R3/R4: a labelled 'Check an address' box (placeholder 'e.g. 600 E Mariposa St, Altadena') runs one popover state machine. Every lookup has a sequence number; Escape, an edit, Clear, an outside or map click, a new selection and a pick close the popover and abort the request, and late replies are dropped. The popover never covers the card: the card is pushed down on desktop and the sheet shortens on phones. On phones, focusing the box closes open sheets and a pick blurs the input. Errors are in plain words. A fire opens only on an exact name (or a bare name when no town has that name), as an explicit open (source 'search', never autoBuild). Other matches are listed as 'Analysis ready' or 'Data not prepared', and an unprepared fire opens the shell's fire card, which asks. The current fire gives 'Showing the Eaton Fire'. C-R5: scripts/build_gazetteer.py builds fire3d/data/gazetteer_ca.json from the 2026 Census Gazetteer (1,622 California places, 1,802 ZCTAs; 131 KB, 46 KB gzipped). /api/geocode answers ZIP codes and towns locally, with no upstream call; a pick flies to an area-sized box and asks for an address or a map click ('town center (approximate)', 'ZIP area (approximate)', Gazetteer credit). O-R9: on the overview, a point shows the official line and the nearest fires measured from CAL FIRE's reported points, with no risk wording, plus 'Zoom to the <fire>' when a prepared fire's area contains it (decision 10). C-R6/C-R7/C-R8: the card leads with four blocks: near here (Mapped/Estimate, age, Stale); official information, always present via useOfficialAtPoint; the model as a dated sentence in Public (Command keeps the figure, run line and quantiles) plus up to three tagged reasons (wind toward/away/across [Model], dryness as numbers or a Red Flag Warning [Official], uphill of the nearest edge [Terrain data]); and updated and reliability. Details stay one tap away. The coordinate strip follows the shell's variants: full, compact, and a one-line phone form. Decision 10: zoom focus no longer closes the search, the card keeps the point with a loading line, and the official hook stays mounted across focus changes.

API: /api/geocode?q=91001 returns kind zip, near Altadena; q=Altadena returns place; q=Pasadena City Hall returns [] with an explanation; all local (upstream mock saw 0 calls). In the app (API 8713 FIRE3D_LIVE=0, Vite 5183, Playwright Chrome GPU, scratchpad v7/loc/flows.mjs) at 1440x900 and 390x844: (1) /api/geocode delayed 3 s: after Escape the selection stays null; after an edit, null; after a map click, the click's own point is kept and the reply is dropped. (2) 'Malibu' with Eaton open flies to Malibu (z11.8) and only lists the Bryson Fire as 'Data not prepared · opens its card'; 0 /build or /jobs requests in every run; data/incidents still holds only the 10 known bundles. (3) A simulated 504 shows 'The U.S. Census address service did not answer in time. Try again in a moment.'; the popover sits at y 124-184 and the card moves to y 192. (4) Phone with Layers open: focusing the box closes the sheet, results show at y 127-396, and a pick releases focus and flies to Paradise (z11). (5) ZIP 91001 flies to z12.5 (desktop) / z11.7 (phone) with the prompt and Gazetteer credit. (6) Eaton, 600 E Mariposa St: inside the estimated burned area, burned around Jan 8 07:39 PST; archived NWS Red Flag Warning (Los Angeles/Oxnard); model 0 of 31 plus 'The fire reached this spot ... but none of the simulated fires did'; Command shows 0%, the run line and quantiles. (7) Henderson, live with data 18 h old: Stale chip, 1.0 mi east of the estimated burned area, wind 'blowing across', about 270 ft uphill, none listed (checked). (8) Click 5.7 mi south of Eaton's burned area: the outside-the-modeled-area note, and the model says 'Unknown, not low'. (9) Point inside the listed Orange County zone, Evacuation layer OFF: 'Evacuation Order', Orange County, issuer time not given (listed by Cal OES Oct 17 18:01 PDT), 14 mi from the Henderson Fire, 'Cal OES does not say which fire this is for'. (10) Overview: a Glendale address lists Eaton 11 mi E, Palisades 18 mi W, Hurst 18 mi NW and the nearest active fire (Peak, 19 mi E); a point inside Eaton's area at the California view offers 'Zoom to the Eaton Fire'. (11) Decision 10: Henderson, then flying to a point in Norte's area, switched to Norte by zoom (incidentSource 'zoom'); the card kept the point. Card heights at 1440x900: Henderson 673 px, burned home about 800 px (scrolls in its slot), overview 651 px. Final captures: 0 page errors; the one 504 console line is the simulated one. An earlier transient React hooks-order error came from Vite hot updates of other agents' edits during a run (104 hot updates logged); 3 clean reruns had none. Count-only secret scan of my files: 0. My servers (8713, 5183) are stopped.
contract_deviations: CONTRACT §6 /api/geocode, additive: ZIP codes and California towns are matched locally. Replies add 'kind' and 'local'. Each match adds kind, name, place_type, place_type_label, zip, land_km2, exact, near and near_km. Local replies have benchmark null and add 'vintage'. A 5-digit ZIP is no longer a 400, and the endpoint answers 503 when the index is missing.

CONTRACT §5.1 search: 'local incident names -> selectIncident' became: only an exact name (full name, id, or name + year; or the bare name when no town has it) opens the fire, through openFromSearch = setFireCard(null) + selectIncident(id, { source: 'search' }), never autoBuild. Other matches are only listed; an unprepared fire opens its fire card (I3).

Web types: GeocodeResponse.benchmark and AddressDetails.benchmark are string | null; GeocodeMatch gains optional fields; LocationReport gains dryness, edgeRise and latestObservationMs (additive); LineKind gains 'Official' and 'Terrain data'. The card model's 'summary' shape changed (near/reasons/model/run/reliability/keys); only location code reads it.
Address selections: 'label' is the title-cased address ('600 E Mariposa St, Altadena, CA 91001'); 'matchedAddress' keeps the Census text.
The card no longer repeats the point's coordinates (the always-visible strip shows them with copy buttons), and the drag hint lives on the map pin label.
Overview card: 'Zoom to the <fire>' (per the coordinator's decision-10 note) instead of O-R9's 'Open the <name> analysis'.
A change of useStore.incidentId (zoom focus) no longer closes the search popover or cancels a lookup; only explicit actions do.
Public card details drop the word 'hindcast' and the 'Scientific values' section; Command keeps both (C-R8).
known_issues: Card height at the shell's 300 px card width: the most verbose case (inside the burn, an archived Red Flag Warning, the 'model missed' line) is about 800 px and scrolls inside its slot on 1440x900; Henderson is 673 px. In Command the full strip leaves even less room, so the run line and quantiles sit one scroll below the model line. At 360 px the cards would be 712 / 638 px.

official-web's useOfficialContext (web/src/official/hooks.ts) floors the timeline time to the minute. For a live fire whose latest observation is not on a whole minute (Norte when zoom-focused: 00:42:41Z), the floored time is before the now marker, so isPastForCurrentSources says past. The card (and Official now) then say 'Evacuation orders: not shown for past dates' for a live fire. Henderson worked only because its times sit on whole minutes.

Whether an address searched from the overview gets zoom-focused depends on the map's focus rule. In my run, flying to 600 E Mariposa St (inside Eaton's area) stayed on the overview, so the card offered 'Zoom to the Eaton Fire'; flying near Norte did focus it.
lib/geodesy.ts and lib/plainLanguage.ts needed no changes (the timeline already rewords forecastDescription for Public).
notes_for_integrator: 1) .gitignore (root): the first line 'data/' also ignores backend/fire3d/data/, so gazetteer_ca.json is never committed. Add the line '!backend/fire3d/data/' right after 'data/' (checked in a scratch repo: data/incidents stays ignored and the gazetteer is included). Without the file, town and ZIP search answer 503; street addresses still work. 2) web/src/official/hooks.ts, useOfficialContext: compare against a marker floored the same way, e.g. replace 'isPastForCurrentSources(s.mode, timeMs, now, s.marker)' with 'isPastForCurrentSources(s.mode, timeMs, now, s.marker != null ? Math.floor(s.marker / 60_000) * 60_000 : s.marker)', or compare with the unquantised st.timeMs. Otherwise zoom-focused live fires whose latest observation is not on a whole minute hide their evacuation status as a 'past date'. 3) Optional, shell: the card would fit its four blocks with less scrolling if --m-card-w matched the search column (--m-search-w, 380 px; measured 360 px: Henderson 673 to 638 px, burned home about 800 to 712 px). 4) README (not mine): API table row '/api/geocode?q=<US street address | California town | ZIP code>' = 'Census Geocoder matches (cached 30 days); California towns and ZIP areas from the local Census Gazetteer index (no upstream call)'. Data-sources table: add 'U.S. Census Bureau Gazetteer Files (2026: California places and ZCTAs) | town and ZIP search | public domain (U.S. Government work, 17 U.S.C. 105) | credit: U.S. Census Bureau Gazetteer Files'. SPEC (official-backend owns it) could mention the same /api/geocode additions. 5) To rebuild the index: cd backend && uv run python scripts/build_gazetteer.py [--year 2026] (downloads 2 files once through fire3d.http), or --source DIR to use files already downloaded. 6) CONTRACT 13 '### location' documents the endpoint, the search rules, openFromSearch, searchUi (the card yields to the popover), the card blocks and the strip variants.
